repairs.value: Epistemic distance can protect uncoerced commitment only if sincere seekers still receive enough recognizable evidence to know that a divine relationship is genuinely available.

An AI-generated extension could treat divine hiddenness as justified only within a calibrated accessibility constraint. Limited uncertainty may preserve cooperative inquiry, fellowship, and freely formed commitment, but those goods do not require total doubt or permanent nonresistant nonbelief. Because a choice is meaningful only when the relational option is recognizable, every sincere seeker would need proportionate evidence that God exists, is available, and invites relationship. On this model, evidence could vary across persons and circumstances while remaining sufficient for an actionable choice, so hiddenness serves inquiry without erasing the freedom it is meant to protect.
